Safety in Case of Faulty Connections

6.1.1.1 Terminals meant for accepting power or for delivering power to other units shall be so designed as to provide adequate protection against misuse or faulty connection of power cords, plug-i? units or any other auxiliaries proper to the nornial use of the device and carrying sockets and connectors for this purpose, 6.1.1.2 Terminals meant for connection to dc power supply or meant to deliver dc power to other apparatus shqll be marked as to polarity and possible connection to earth or chassis. S.l.l.! Selectors for power supply and output voltage, if meant to be set by the user, shall be maiked with an indication of the kind of Corilpliance shall be checked by power supply and voltage concerned. inspection. 6.1.1.4 For amplifiers designed to be mounted in racks or enclosures, it is recommended that a check be made as to whether the terminals meant to be internally connected to `the wiring in the enclosure are unambiguously identifiable, either by marking or by virtue of their position, with respect to the instructions for connection in the installation manual, it being assumed that these are to be read by skilled personnel. 7. conditions.

By keeping all other setting for rated conditions, source e m f ( 1 kHz ) shall be adjusted so that rated total harmonic distortion is obtained. The output power is noted in this condition. Frequency of the source shall be varied, both on higher and lower side of 1 kHz, keeping total harmonic distortion constant at its rated value, reducing source e m f, if necessary to meet this total harmonic distortion. A graph shall be plotted giving output power in dB relative to the rated output power on Y axis and frequency' on X axis ( Log Scale ). This is termed output power vs frequency at constant total harmonic distortion'. 6
